clue.text: Old wine put back in container for spirit

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed pieces go inside the container word

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: put back signals the old-wine pair is read backwards

parts.note: Medoc is a red wine from Bordeaux

explanation.surface: Someone decants an aged wine back into a vessel meant for liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses the old-wine pair and 'in' places that run inside the container; 'spirit' reads as drink in the surface but means a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cacodemon is an evil spirit or demon, from Greek for bad demon.

clue.text: Treatment of news makes man express IS anger

clue.text: Artist shows bird crossing river

indicators.note: the bird crosses over the river, so the river letter sits inside it

parts.note: a coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: A painter depicts a waterbird flying over a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Corot was a 19th-century French landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot is a famous French painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Violent rebel said to be handsome maybe

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fierce insurgent is reputed to be good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Violent' rearranges REBEL SAID; 'said to be' reads like a hint of a homophone but 'said' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone handsome is an example of a person found attractive or worth having.

clue.text: Yours truly has a den that's 5 most squalid

parts.note: yours truly is the setter, so me
a nest is a den or lair

explanation.surface: The speaker admits to owning the filthiest hideaway around.
explanation.walkthrough: The '5' in the clue as held is an OCR stray from the page and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe a poor, shabby place, so the superlative is the most squalid.

clue.text: Can't use darts? One may finish in the DOOR madhouse

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Can't use darts? One may finish in the DOOR madhouse', carries an OCR stray 'DOOR'; the anagram of CANT USE is clear but the exact printed wording cannot be recovered from the unreadable scan.
annotationWithheld.clue: Can't use darts? One may finish in the DOOR madhouse

clue.text: During breather, right to keep on with questions?

indicators.note: during places the right letter within the breather word

parts.note: a gill is the organ a fish breathes through

explanation.surface: Someone pauses for breath and the interrogator resumes.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrogate someone relentlessly is a figurative sense of cooking under intense heat.

clue.text: Bleak birthplace of Edward's son

definitions.meaning: John of ..., son of Edward III, was born in Ghent, anglicised as this name

explanation.surface: A dreary town where a royal prince was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak and haggard are near synonyms; the old English name of Ghent gave John of Gaunt his title.

clue.text: Naughty behaviour at home love to get in Christmas spirit?

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the love letter is put inside the festive pair

parts.note: DEC is short for December, the Christmas month
rum is a spirit
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Misbehaving indoors with affection and too much festive drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get in' puts the love letter between the two halves of what looks like one festive phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper behaviour lacking decency or good manners.

clue.text: Run a sort of tournament

definitions.meaning: a run in stockings or tights is a vertical tear
a competition where players challenge those ranked just above them

explanation.surface: A race is staged as a kind of contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is both a tear in hosiery and a ranked challenge competition.

clue.text: Morality half rejected by American agent with bad influence

indicators.note: half of the morality word is thrown away

parts.note: virtue is morality
US means American

explanation.surface: An American spy whose morals have slipped is a corrupting presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half rejected' drops TUE from VIRTUE, leaving VIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is an infectious agent, and figuratively any corrupting influence.

clue.text: A good person 'arassed and disconcerted

parts.note: ST stands for saint, a good person
harassed with its H dropped Cockney-style means hounded with its H dropped

explanation.surface: A kindly soul is pestered and thrown off balance.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''arassed' tells you to drop the H of its synonym HOUNDED too.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounded and disconcerted both describe being shocked and thrown off balance.

clue.text: One no longer working about to go to island

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Tiree is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A pensioner is about to head off to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to go' looks like a phrase meaning 'soon to leave', but 'about' is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiree is a person who has stopped working, a synonym of pensioner.

clue.text: Aggressive action curtailed by ambassador and one of his staff

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the final letter, is cut

parts.note: an attack is aggressive action
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: Hostilities are cut short by an envoy and his aide.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior diplomat on an ambassador's staff.

clue.text: Obeys those running the company and is ignored

definitions.meaning: read literally, follows the rules of the directors

explanation.surface: Someone toes the line at work yet goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be discarded or disregarded; literally it reads as following the directors.

clue.text: One brought up to protect firm, Scrooge endlessly cut costs

indicators.note: the reversed word guards the firm inside it
in a down clue, brought up reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
CO is short for company, a firm
a Scrooge is a miser, after Dickens's character

explanation.surface: Scrooge, sheltering his company, slashes spending without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses ONE to ENO; 'to protect' puts the firm inside that; 'endlessly' trims the last letter off the miser.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to reduce spending, a synonym of cutting costs.

clue.text: To tour province old doctor employs public transport

indicators.note: the old doctor goes around the province, which ends up inside

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
NI is Northern Ireland, the province
uses means employs

explanation.surface: An elderly GP travels round the region by bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To tour' wraps the old doctor around the region; Northern Ireland is often called 'the Province' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnibuses, the full word for buses, are a form of public transport.

clue.text: Shrub to tilt falling into foreign river

indicators.note: the tilt word drops inside the river

parts.note: the Oder is a river in central Europe
to lean is to tilt

explanation.surface: A bush leans over and topples into a river abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen flowering shrub of Mediterranean origin.

clue.text: Cat perhaps means Matilda's no mice running around

indicators.note: running around shows the letters dashing into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of the name with its S kept as fodder

explanation.surface: A girl's pet cat is useless, with no mice scurrying about.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is an example of a tame household pet.

clue.text: Volunteers charge exorbitantly for event with wine

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve volunteers
to sting someone is to overcharge them

explanation.surface: Reservists are overcharged for a drinks evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasting is a gathering where wines are sampled.

clue.text: Is individual performance about to upend big figures?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upend turns the whole run upwards

parts.note: a solo is a performance by one
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A soloist wonders whether to overturn giant statues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to upend' reverses IS + SOLO + C, giving the plural of COLOSSUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are giant statues, or figuratively very great people.

clue.text: Wise man restricts religious chatterer.. led

indicators.note: restricts means holds in, so the religious letters go inside

parts.note: a mage is a magus, a wise man
PI is short for pious, religious

explanation.surface: A sage keeps a devout follower under control.
explanation.walkthrough: The '.. led' in the clue as held is an OCR stray and does no work.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a noisy bird, so the name is used for a chatterer.

clue.text: More than one animal is put down after a disease

indicators.note: is is written down after the other pieces

parts.note: gout is a disease of the joints

explanation.surface: Several beasts are destroyed after an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' suggests putting animals to sleep, but it means 'written after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Agoutis are South American rodents, so the plural means more than one animal.

clue.text: "Here's to a very good chap!"

parts.note: ST is saint, a very good man

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to a fine fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Here's to someone is the formula of a toast, a drink in their honour.

clue.text: Insect's parts found in scientific workplace by woman

parts.note: lab is short for laboratory
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Bits of a bug are found in a laboratory by a female researcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Labella are lip-like mouthparts of insects; the singular is labellum.

clue.text: Bishop entertained by unordained per is a happy man

indicators.note: the bishop is hosted inside the unordained word

parts.note: lay means not ordained into the clergy
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A bishop is welcomed by a contented layperson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy as Larry' is a British idiom. The 'per' in the clue as held is an OCR stray.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'happy as Larry' makes the name stand for a very happy man.

clue.text: Sign to join formal schools

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A star sign is attached to stiff institutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Primaries are primary schools for younger children.

clue.text: Girl's brought back instrument from India

indicators.note: brought back reads the possessive name backwards

parts.note: Dora's, with the S of the possessive kept

explanation.surface: A girl returns home with an Indian instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sarod is a stringed lute-like instrument of Indian classical music.

clue.text: Permission for absence facilitates a time by the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A leave pass lets someone spend time by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is a school or college pass to be away; 'facilitates' acts as a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeat is Latin for 'let him go out', a formal leave of absence.

clue.text: One contradicting philosopher wins at the outset

parts.note: gains means wins; at the outset says this piece comes first
A J Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker who starts by winning arguments argues back.
explanation.definitionFit: A gainsayer is someone who denies or contradicts.
